title: CRLR/164/2005 of HARISH CHANDRA  ARYA Vs STATE and ORS.

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 164 of 2005
Harish Chandra Arya ............. Revisionist
 versus
State and others ............. Respondents
Mr. Rajesh Joshi, Advocate holding brief of Mr. Rajendra Tamta,
Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. P.S. Saun, AGA for the respondent State.
Mr. D.S. Mehta, Advocate for respondents no. 2 to 7.
Hon'ble U.C. Dhyani, J. (oral)

Informant Harish Chandra Arya lodged an
FIR on 04.05.2001, in police station Lalkuan, District
Nainital, enumerating the facts contained therein that he
belongs to a community of Scheduled Caste and was
working in the Century Paper Mill, Lalkuan. Informant
was residing in an official accommodation, near VIP
Gate, allotted to him by his employer. On 01.05.2001,
at about 06:30 A.M., when the informant was returning
from the factory to his house, some antisocial elements
used casteist remarks against him. Vikram Singh, Ajay
Sony, Vijay Sony, Dharmendra Mishra, Manoj Kumar
and Chandra Shakher alongwith 8-10 more people
assaulted informant Harish Chandra Arya with kicks,
fists and sticks. The informant fell down on the ground.
Vikram Singh and Ajay Sony exhorted that the
informant should be killed and thrown into river Gola.
Many a people assembled there and intervened. Injured
was taken to dispensary of Lalkuan Century Paper Mill.

2
Considering the serious condition of the informant, he
was referred to Soban Singh Jeena Base Hospital,
Haldwani.
2) On the basis of the complaint of informant
Harish Chandra Arya, police registered case crime no.
342 of 2001 under Sections 147, 323, 504, 506 of IPC
read with Section 3(2)(v) of the Scheduled Castes and
Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.
After investigation, a chargesheet was submitted
against the accused persons in respect of offences
punishable under Sections 147, 307 / 149, 506 of IPC
and under Section 3(1)(v) of the Scheduled Castes and
Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.
The Special Court took the cognizance on the
chargesheet and after hearing the accused persons,
charged them for the offences complained of against
them. All of them pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
3) PW1 Harish Chandra Arya
(complainant/injured), PW2 Anokhey Lal Gangwar
(eyewitness), PW3 Chandan Singh (eyewitness), PW4
Navin Chand, PW5 H.C. Mahesh Pal, PW6 S.I.
Narayan Singh (Investigating Officer) and PW7 Dr. M.
Anwar (Medical Officer) were examined on behalf of
the prosecution. Dr. P.C. Pheloria was summoned by
the Special Court under Section 311 of Cr.P.C. Dr.
P.C. Pheloria was thus examined as court witness. Chik
FIR (Ext. Ka-2), copy of GD (Ext. Ka-3), site plan (Ext.

3
Ka-4), chargesheet (Ext. Ka-5), injury report (Ext. Ka-7), copy of ultrasound (Ext. Ka-8) and supplementary
injury report (Ext. Ka-9) were proved on behalf of the
prosecution. Incriminating evidence was put to the
accused persons under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. in which
they said that they were falsely implicated in the case.
No evidence was given in defence. After examining the
evidence on record, learned Special Judge acquitted
accused persons of the charges under Sections 307 /
149, 506 of IPC and Section 3(2)(v) of the Scheduled
Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities)
Act, 1989. Accused persons were however convicted
for the offences punishable under Section 323 / 149
and 147 of IPC. Aggrieved against the said order,
complainant Harish Chandra Arya moved the criminal
revision before this Court, which was numbered as
CRLR No. 164 of 2005.
4) It is the contention of learned counsel for the
revisionist that the injuries sustained by the revisionist
were fatal in nature and one of them was dangerous to
life. The intestine of the revisionist was operated upon.
Surgeon, who operated the intestine, said that there was
continuous discharge and there was deposition of blood
in some part of intestine. The contention of learned
counsel for the revisionist is that the nature of injuries
was so grievous that the accused were having the
knowledge that such injuries were likely to cause death
of the informant. It is further submitted that learned

4
Special Court has committed error by not convicting the
accused persons either under Section 307 of IPC or
under Section 308 of IPC. Learned trial court also
ought to have convicted the accused persons under
Section 3(2)(v) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled
Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989. It may be
mentioned here that no appeal was preferred on behalf
of the convicts against their conviction under Sections
323 / 149 and 147 of IPC. It may also be mentioned at
this stage that the accused persons were granted benefit
of Section 4 of Probation of Offenders Act, 1958. They
were released on probation for their good conduct for a
period of one year and were directed to furnish bond of
Rs. 10,000/- each before the Probation Officer. They
were also directed to maintain peace and be of good
behaviour. It was made clear by the learned Addl.
Sessions Judge that if, during the period of one year, the
accused persons were found to have committed any act
in violation of their bonds, they will be dealt with as per
the provisions of Probation of Offenders Act, 1958 to
serve out the sentence.
5) Learned court below has highlighted the
submissions made by learned counsel for the accused
persons before him and dealt with those submissions
appropriately. When complainant Harish Chandra Arya
was examined by the Medical Officer of Soban Singh
Jeena Base Hospital, Haldwani on 01.06.2001, at 12:40

5
P.M., he found following injury on his person as per the
injury report (Ext. Ka-7):
"(1) Hitting bluntly by someone.
 Complaint of pain all over the abdomen without
 having any external mark of injury.
 Complaint of pain all over left thigh without
 having any external mark of injury.
 Opinion :- No definite opinion can be given about
 the cause, duration and nature of injury as there
 were no external mark of injury. Hence, the
 patient hospitalized, kept under observation and
 referred to surgeon and orthopedic surgeon for
 expert opinion on the respective injuries.
Advised x-ray abdomen (erect posture) for nature
 of injury no. 1".
6) The Medical Officer also submitted
supplementary report (Ext. Ka-9). As per supplementary
report, the patient was hospitalized, kept under
observation and referred to surgeon for expert opinion.
The surgeon advised ultrasound of whole abdomen for
ascertaining cause and nature of injury no. 1.
7) As per Radiologist's report dated
03.05.2001:
Ultrasound whole abdomen reveals - free fluid
noted in peritoneal space, low level echogenecity.
8) As per Surgeon's report -absolute
constipation were the symptoms on exploration of

6
abdomen, large haematoma of the ascending colour
detected.
9) Regarding nature of injury, the injury was
blunt abdominal injury. Grievous in nature. Opinion -
"hence the injury no. 1 was caused by blunt hard object
and was grievous in nature."
10) In view of the nature of injuries sustained by
the injured can it be said that the learned court below
awarded inadequate sentence to the accused persons?
The reply is - an emphatic 'No'. If the accused persons
were convicted under Sections 323 / 149 and 147 of
IPC, learned trial court has not committed any illegality
in passing such sentence as was awarded to the accused
persons vide order dated 20.08.2005. It was hardly a
case in which the trial court could entertain the idea that
the accused persons did any act with such intention or
knowledge, and under such circumstances, that if they
by that act caused death, they would be guilty of
murder or culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
In other words, the trial court has committed no error
by holding that no offence punishable under Section
307 / 149 of IPC was established against the accused
persons. Learned trial court has discussed the evidence
tendered by the prosecution witnesses, duly supported
by medical evidence and has rightly come to the
conclusion that the offence punishable under Sections
323 / 149 and 147 of IPC, and not under Sections 307 /

7
149 and 506 of IPC were established against the
accused persons. Learned court below has also
committed no mistake by holding that no offence
punishable under Section 3(2)(v) of the Scheduled
Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities)
Act, 1989 was proved against the accused persons, the
reasons whereof are assigned in internal page 12 and 13
of the impugned judgment. Considering the facts and
circumstances of the case, any finding contrary to the
findings of learned court below, would have been
perverse.
11) The criminal revision lacks merit and the
same is dismissed.
12) Let a copy of this judgment alongwith lower
court records be sent back to the court below.
